methods.label: Match cell colors with number parity
methods.explanation:
Color the four corners and the center black, and color the other four cells white. Every move across a shared edge changes color.

Now follow the cells containing \(1,2,\ldots,9\). At each step, both the cell color and the odd/even status of the label change, so their correspondence stays the same. Thus \(1,3,5,7,9\) all occupy one color, while \(2,4,6,8\) occupy the other.

There are five odd labels, so their color must be black, which has five cells. Therefore the four corners and center contain exactly the odd numbers, whose sum is
\[
1+3+5+7+9=25.
\]
Subtracting the given corner sum leaves \(25-18=7\) in the center.

For example, the arrangement
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
1&2&3\\
8&7&4\\
9&6&5
\end{array}
\]
satisfies every adjacency condition and has corner sum \(18\), confirming that the forced value is attainable. The center is \(7\), choice C.
